questions.question_text: What are the radius, domain, and range of the semicircle $y = -\sqrt{36 - x^2}$?

options.why: Gave the range of the upper semicircle instead of the lower semicircle.
Used $r = 36$ instead of taking the square root $r = \sqrt{36} = 6$.
Gave the domain and range of the right semicircle instead of the lower semicircle.

questions.solution_text:
$r = \sqrt{36} = 6$.
The negative sign before the root indicates a lower semicircle ($y \le 0$).
Domain: $[-6, 6]$
Range: $[-6, 0]$

options.why: Chose the upper semicircle instead of the graphed lower semicircle.
Made $x$ the subject, giving the left semicircle instead of the lower semicircle.
Used the radius $8$ instead of $r^2 = 64$ under the square root.

questions.solution_text:
The graph is a lower semicircle with radius $r = 8$, so $r^2 = 64$.
Use $y = -\sqrt{r^2 - x^2}$.
$y = -\sqrt{64 - x^2}$

questions.solution_text:

questions.question_text: What are the domain and range of the upper semicircle $y = \sqrt{100 - x^2}$?

options.why: Forgot to take the square root of $100$ to find the radius $10$.
Swapped the domain and range of the upper semicircle.
Gave the range for the lower semicircle instead of the upper semicircle.

questions.solution_text:
Radius $r = \sqrt{100} = 10$.
Upper semicircle $\implies$ Domain $[-10, 10]$ and Range $[0, 10]$.

options.why: Chose the lower half instead of the graphed upper half.
Made $x$ the subject, giving the right half instead of the upper half.
Used the radius $6$ instead of $r^{2} = 36$ under the square root.

questions.solution_text:
The graph is an upper semicircle with radius $6$.
Use $y = \sqrt{r^2-x^2}$ with $r^2 = 36$.
$y = \sqrt{36-x^2}$

questions.question_text: What are the exact domain and range of the semicircle $y = -\sqrt{\frac{11}{4} - x^2}$?

options.why: Gave the range of the upper semicircle instead of the lower semicircle.
Used $r^2 = \frac{11}{4}$ as the radius instead of taking its square root.
Took the square root of the numerator but left the denominator as $4$ instead of using $\sqrt{4}=2$.

questions.solution_text:
$r = \sqrt{\frac{11}{4}} = \frac{\sqrt{11}}{2}$.
The negative sign gives a lower semicircle.
Domain: $\left[-\frac{\sqrt{11}}{2},\frac{\sqrt{11}}{2}\right]$
Range: $\left[-\frac{\sqrt{11}}{2},0\right]$
